source.title: Neural Active Learning on Heteroskedastic Distributions
source.authors: Savya Khosla; Chew Kin Whye; Jordan T. Ash; Cyril Zhang; Kenji Kawaguchi; Alex Lamb

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper and appendix; no material cutoff is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports loss behavior on randomly labeled examples mixed with clean data. It describes noisy examples converging to a suboptimal solution, qualifying the claim in this heteroskedastic setting. It does not test training on an entirely randomly labeled dataset.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports accuracy and clean-example selection results for active-learning methods, but those do not measure fitting random labels. Figure 6's gradient magnitudes are not a measure of fitting error.
record.test_reason: The study measures active-learning performance and loss on mixed clean data and repeated noisy inputs with conflicting labels. These losses do not establish training classification error on a completely random labeling, or later memorization of noise. Its noise construction differs materially from assigning random labels to distinct training examples.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: uncertainty-based active learning can fail on heteroskedastic distributions by oversampling noisy examples, and diversity sampling, fine-tuning, and LHD can mitigate these failures.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses active learning on mixed clean and heteroskedastic noisy data, measuring loss curves during training; it does not train on a fully randomly labeled dataset as in the original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: The measured noisy-example loss is reported across three noise constructions: noisy-blank, noisy-diverse, and noisy-class.

fits_no_version.finding: During first-round CIFAR10 training, noisy-example loss quickly plateaus at a suboptimal solution while clean-example loss continues falling. The authors attribute this to conflicting labels for repeated inputs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: On these heteroskedastic datasets containing repeated inputs with conflicting labels, ResNet18 reduces clean-example loss while noisy-example loss remains high.

record.code_released: URL stated as “this URL” in the supplied text; no address is given.
record.problems: The loss-curve results are figure-only with no numeric values or stated uncertainty. The study uses mixed clean and noisy data, so it does not establish whether a network can fit a fully randomly labeled training set.
record.rows_left_out: No other reported results directly measure fitting randomly labeled examples; active-learning accuracy, selection percentages, timing, and gradient magnitudes were left out because they do not measure that behavior.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training error on a completely randomly labeled training set, chance test error, and unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters.
Training time to fit random versus true labels and convergence slowing with increasing label corruption. Active-learning runtime comparisons do not measure these.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs to zero training error.

Perfect training fit and steadily increasing test error across corruption fractions from zero to all. Table 5 measures active-learning accuracy at selected pool-noise fractions, with acquisition changing the training composition.
Whether explicit regularization prevents random-label fitting, and whether removing regularization harms true-label generalization.
Learning shared real-data patterns before subsequently memorizing noisy labels. The reported noisy losses remain high; subsequent memorization is not demonstrated.

record.verdict_notes: The loss observations are valid results, but their links to V1 and their reversed states are unsupported. Neither the noisy loss plateau nor the difference between clean and noisy loss trajectories warrants a verdict on the listed versions.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests randomly labeled examples mixed with clean data, not a training set whose labels are all random. It does not report training error or test error for a fully random labeling, or compare training hyperparameters with true-label training.
